findings.title: robots.txt Presence & Accessibility

evidence.error: robots.txt was not found or returned non-200 status code

findings.why_it_matters: robots.txt is the universal entry point for all web crawlers. Without it, crawlers may waste crawl budget on non-canonical URLs, internal search parameters, or private endpoints.
findings.fix: Publish a valid /robots.txt file at the root of your domain.

findings.title: Accidental Critical Path Blocking in robots.txt

evidence.message: No catastrophic global Disallow: / rule found.

findings.why_it_matters: Accidental 'Disallow: /' or disallowing core CSS/JS/images prevents search engines and AI crawlers from indexing content or rendering pages properly.
findings.fix: Audit Disallow rules in robots.txt to ensure the homepage ('/') and primary content paths remain accessible.

findings.title: XML Sitemap Discovery & Validity

evidence.error: No valid XML sitemaps discovered or sitemap was empty

findings.why_it_matters: XML sitemaps provide a roadmap of all canonical, high-value pages, ensuring search engines discover new and updated content rapidly.
findings.fix: Publish an XML sitemap at /sitemap.xml and reference it in /robots.txt.

findings.title: www vs. non-www Redirection Consistency
findings.why_it_matters: Allowing both www and non-www versions of a website to return 200 OK splits link authority and creates duplicate content across domains.
findings.fix: Configure web server or CDN (Cloudflare/Vercel) to redirect the non-canonical host with a 301 status.

findings.title: Missing rel='canonical' Link Tag

evidence.error: No rel='canonical' tag found in page HTML

findings.why_it_matters: Without an explicit canonical tag, search engines must guess which version of a page to index, leading to duplicate content dilution across trailing slashes, HTTP/HTTPS, and query params.
findings.fix: Add a self-referencing <link rel='canonical' href='https://...'> tag in the <head>.

findings.title: Missing or Empty <title> Tag

evidence.error: Title tag is missing or whitespace only

findings.why_it_matters: The <title> tag is one of the most critical on-page ranking signals and provides the clickable headline in search engine results and AI answer cards.
findings.fix: Add a unique, descriptive <title> tag inside the <head> of every HTML page.

findings.title: Missing Meta Description
findings.why_it_matters: Meta descriptions provide the summary snippet in search results and help AI crawlers understand page intent before full parsing.
findings.fix: Add an enticing, descriptive <meta name='description' content='...'> tag.

findings.title: Missing <h1> heading tag

evidence.error: No <h1> heading tag found in page HTML

findings.why_it_matters: Every indexable page should have exactly one descriptive <h1> tag serving as the main topic header for users, search crawlers, and screen readers.
findings.fix: Ensure each page contains exactly one <h1> element accurately describing the page subject.

findings.title: Core Schema.org Type Coverage
findings.why_it_matters: No Schema.org entity types were detected on this page.
findings.fix: Deploy relevant Schema.org JSON-LD templates based on page intent.

findings.title: Time to First Byte (TTFB) Latency
findings.why_it_matters: High server response latency slows down crawling, burns crawl budget, degrades Core Web Vitals, and causes AI bots with short timeout thresholds (e.g. 800ms) to abort requests.
findings.fix: Optimize database queries, enable server-side caching, and utilize edge CDNs (Cloudflare/Fastly).

findings.title: Mobile Responsive Viewport Configuration

evidence.error: No valid viewport meta tag found

findings.why_it_matters: Mobile-first indexing requires a responsive viewport tag so pages render correctly across smartphones, tablets, and mobile crawlers.
findings.fix: Add <meta name='viewport' content='width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0'> in the <head>.

findings.title: Missing recommended security headers (HSTS / nosniff)
findings.why_it_matters: Security headers (HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options) protect visitors from clickjacking, MIME sniffing, and man-in-the-middle downgrade attacks.
findings.fix: Configure web server or CDN to send Strict-Transport-Security and X-Content-Type-Options headers.
